projection.growthBasis: Historical publisher forecast held constant for illustration. In January 2024, H2 Gambling Capital forecast approximately USD 573 billion in 2024 global gross win for regulated white/grey gambling markets, from an estimated USD 536 billion in 2023 and approximately 7% expected growth. This is operator gross win (stakes less payouts), not turnover, a confirmed 2024 result, all illegal gambling, or a 2026 forecast.

source: H2 Gambling Capital — January 2024 forecast for 2024 gross win

sources.name: RAND — Evaluation of Housing for Health Permanent Supportive Housing Program, Table 3.11 (2017)

categories.methodology: Historical Los Angeles Housing for Health benchmark: RAND's 2017 report lists USD 16,035 as the median annual programme cost among 890 participants in the first year after housing (Table 3.11). Covers housing subsidy and case-management services; excludes administrative costs and construction or acquisition of housing. This is a local study-era operating-cost reference, not a 2026 US or worldwide housing price.

sources.name: United for Global Mental Health — US$200 billion financing gap report
United for Global Mental Health — Financing of mental health: the current situation and ways forward (full report)

categories.methodology: United for Global Mental Health's 2023 report estimates a global annual gap of at least USD 200 billion in domestic public financing for mental health. It compares government spending with the 2018 Lancet Commission targets: at least 5% of domestic health budgets in low- and middle-income countries and 10% in high-income countries. These budget-share targets are not country-by-country costings of all care needs. The comparison uses a historical lower-bound funding benchmark, not a precise current-year budget or a guarantee that all mental-health needs can be met.

sources.name: HHS — SAMHSA Awards $255 Million to Administer 988 Lifeline

categories.methodology: On 15 May 2026, HHS/SAMHSA announced a USD 255 million award to Vibrant Emotional Health to administer the US 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. The announcement does not establish that this award equals one year of all national and local 988 costs. The comparison counts award-size funding equivalents, not years of operating the whole network or lives saved.

sources.name: Ceres2030 — Sustainable Solutions to End Hunger, Summary Report

categories.methodology: Ceres2030's 2020 model estimated average additional public spending of USD 33 billion per year through 2030: USD 14 billion from donors plus USD 19 billion from low- and middle-income governments. The scenario combines reducing hunger, doubling small-producer incomes and limiting agricultural emissions; it assumes coordinated interventions and induced private investment. This is a historical model benchmark, not a current funding quote or a guarantee that money alone ends hunger.

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene, Summary Report

categories.methodology: World Bank 2016 baseline estimate of USD 37.6 billion per year in 2015 prices for capital investment to extend safely managed drinking-water services to unserved populations in 140 countries during 2015–2030. This is the drinking-water component only; it excludes the additional ongoing operating and maintenance budget and is not an updated 2026 estimate.
